svg.title: One results paragraph before and after revision. Before, 59 words: it opens with filler (it is worth noting that, due to the fact that), hides who did what in the passive, calls app B three different names (the application, the tool, the program), and buries the actual result, 22 of 28 days, at the very end without the baseline's score. After, 36 words: the result comes first with its baseline (22 of 28 days against 17), then the test (p about 0.09), then what follows (a longer study is needed). Same facts, about 40 percent fewer words
svg.text: It is worth noting that, due to the fact that the forecasts were collected over a relatively
short period of time, it was not possible for a statistically significant difference to be
established between the application and the guess, although the tool did appear to perform
quite well, with the program being correct on 22 of the 28 days.
• filler: "it is worth noting", "due to the fact that", "quite"
• one thing, three names: application, tool, program
• the result comes last, with no baseline score
App B was right about rain on 22 of 28 days, against 17 for the "like today" guess. Over
four weeks, this lead was not statistically significant (p ≈ 0.09), so a longer study is
• then the test, then what follows
